messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable 3D 1v1 Rocket League-style game against a bot, first to 3 goals.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js game in `index.html`.
- Chose a neon cyan/orange arena presentation with HUD, menu overlay, mobile controls, bot AI, boost, jumping, goals, scoring, pause, and rematch flow.
- Used Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.161.0/build/three.module.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a large `index.html` containing:
  - Full-screen responsive styling and HUD.
  - Start menu and gameplay overlay.
  - Arena geometry, turf, boards, glass, goals, lights, stands, audience lights, and pitch markings.
  - Player and bot car construction.
  - Ball construction.
  - Initial game state, player movement, boost, jump, bot movement, collision, and scoring helper functions.
- Added mobile touch-control markup and CSS.
- Added desktop keyboard control labels and pause button.
- Added score display for both teams and first-to-three visual indicators.

### Active
- Finish the JavaScript implementation in `index.html`; the file currently ends around line 71 during `driveCar(...)`.
- Add remaining gameplay functions and closing HTML/script tags.
- Run the app and browser checks, then fix runtime/syntax issues.
- Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `index.html` is incomplete and currently has no closing gameplay loop or closing `</script></body></html>` tags.
- A subsequent edit attempt failed with: `Could not find oldString in index.html. It must match exactly, including whitespace and indentation.`

## Next Move
1. Open the remainder of `index.html` after line 71 and append the missing functions.
2. Complete `playGoalSound`, `scoreGoal`, `showEnd`, `updateBall`, particles, pause/menu handlers, keyboard/touch listeners, animation loop, resize handler, and closing tags.
3. Start the project using the repository’s normal start workflow.
4. Use Playwright to verify the start screen and active gameplay, save the latest screenshot as a small `.jpg`, and inspect it.
5. Fix any browser console/runtime errors and summarize assumptions and controls.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main and currently incomplete implementation of the game.
- `README.md`: Project metadata and links.
- `start.sh`: Existing project start entrypoint.
- `capture.sh`: Existing capture entrypoint.

## Important Context
- The game uses a field with the player starting near `z=22`, bot near `z=-22`, and goals at both ends.
- Player controls are intended to be WASD/arrows, `SHIFT` boost, `SPACE` jump, and `P`/Escape pause.
- The HTML already contains DOM IDs expected by the gameplay code, including `#overlay`, `#play-button`, `#pause-button`, `#player-score`, `#bot-score`, `#clock`, `#boost-value`, `#boost-meter`, `#speed-value`, and `#goalflash`.
- The current `index.html` has all initial markup/style and substantial Three.js scene/game setup, but no complete runnable document yet.
